instagram_title: Same Print, Different Brightness on 2 T-Shirts? The Yarn Explains It
notes: Checked: both sha256 values match (bb35148f...). Loudness is -15.7 LUFS and true peak -4.1 dBTP. The audio and visual machine reviews both passed. Cover: the complete question 'SAME PRINT रंग अलग क्यों?' over one relevant picture of folded plain tees in different colours. No person or face, no warehouse or factory scene, no numbers. Allowed for a lesson with no simple comparison. Hook 'YARN / DECIDES PRINT BRIGHTNESS' is readable, fits the first spoken sentence, and is supported by the fact (brightness is very sensitive to yarn lustre). The Sale91.com watermark sits small at the top left with nothing over it. Scenes (sheet, every second, plus the 6 large frames) show plain tees on shelves, on a workbench and on a hanger rack. No hands, no garbled text, no printed result, nothing false. The 4 failed AI clips were replaced with clean stills. Captions match the speech. This is not a DTF lesson, so the 'Sale91.com - MOQ sirf 10 pieces' strip and end card are correct. The transcript has every sentence of script.voice in order and ends on the complete line 'Bas itna hi'. Facts: the script matches print_colour_yarn_hairiness_lustre (printed from one side; lustre, twist and hairiness change the result; higher lustre gives brighter colour; high twist hinders paste penetration). It names no blank or brand, gives no way to judge lustre by eye or touch, and makes no colourfastness promise, DTF claim or price. The YouTube title, description and tags are fine. I corrected the Instagram title: 'Yarn Lustre Check You Missed' suggests a lustre check the buyer can do, which the fact limits forbid, and 'Different Color' misstates the lesson, which is about brightness.
